test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Three circular plates of radii 3 m, 2 m, and 1 m are cut from a rectangular cardboard sheet 46 m long and 8 m wide. If the area of ​​the remaining cardboard sheet is equal to the area of ​​a square, find the length of each side of the square. (Use pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
**Given:**

Length of rectangle = 46 m

Breadth of rectangle = 8 m

Radii of circles = 3 m, 2 m, 1 m

π = 22/7

**Formula used:**

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

Area of circle = π × r²

Area of square = side²

**Calculation:**

Area of rectangle = 46 × 8

⇒ Area of rectangle = 368 m²

Area of circle (r = 3 m) = 22/7 × 3² = 22/7 × 9

⇒ Area = 198/7 m²

Area of circle (r = 2 m) = 22/7 × 2² = 22/7 × 4

⇒ Area = 88/7 m²

Area of circle (r = 1 m) = 22/7 × 1² = 22/7 × 1

⇒ Area = 22/7 m²

Total area of 3 circles = 198/7 + 88/7 + 22/7

⇒ Total area of 3 circles = 308/7 m²

⇒ Total area of 3 circles = 44 m²

Remaining area = Area of rectangle − Total area of circles

⇒ Remaining area = 368 − 44

⇒ Remaining area = 324 m²

Let side of square = a

Area of square = a² = 324

⇒ a² = 324

⇒ a = 18 m

**∴ Length of each side of the square = 18 m**
